title: School district budgets that forecast deficits the books did not show
question: How do the school district’s budgeted general-fund balances compare with what its later forms report for the same year?
finding: The June 2024 budget forecast the general fund would end 2024-25 at $187.1 million after a $148.5 million drawdown; a year later the estimate was $295.9 million, and the June 2026 forms put the unaudited balance at $428.9 million, $241.9 million more than budgeted. For 2023-24 the estimate of $335.6 million became $473.9 million unaudited ($138.3 million more).
how: Form 01 (General Fund) of three budgets: the budget-year ending balance (column F), the next year’s estimated actual ending balance for the same year (column C), and the unaudited July 1 beginning balance two years on (column C, line F1a).
limits: Budgets are meant to be cautious, and late State money or unspent restricted grants raise year-end balances. The unaudited balance can still change on audit. The State fiscal team’s repeated finding that actual revenue and spending are out of line with the budget (in the case file) is the official reading; these figures show its size.
